summary.title: Examples of Great URL Design
summary.one_liner: Learn what makes URLs well designed for both humans and machines, using real examples from StackOverflow, Slack, Jessica Hische, GitHub, and npm.
takeaways: A URL can combine a unique ID for the server with an optional human-readable slug for people.
Sentence-style URLs (like slack.com/is/team-communication) can carry marketing or story language into the address itself.
URLs that map to a product's domain semantics, such as GitHub compare ranges or npm package versions, let users navigate without using the UI.
Trade-offs exist: optional slugs can be changed or misused to mislead while the link still works.
summary.summary: The post, a blog article by Jim Nielsen, builds on Kyle Aster's 2010 point that URLs are the universal syntax of the web. It walks through several examples of URL design it admires: StackOverflow's ID plus optional slug pattern, Slack's sentence-style /is/ URLs, Jessica Hische's third-person sentence URLs on a .is domain, and product URLs from GitHub, npm, and unpkg that mirror their domain concepts. It briefly notes trade-offs, such as slugs that can be used deceptively, and closes by inviting readers to share their own favorites.
